units.source_text: 年幼无知的我，不仅十分信任叔叔，还总是怀着感激之情，把叔叔当作了不起的人来尊敬。

en.t: Young and ignorant as I was, I not only trusted my uncle completely, but always respected him with gratitude as a remarkable man.

units.source_text: 叔叔是个企业家，还做了县议会议员。

en.t: My uncle was a businessman, and he also served as a county assembly member.

units.source_text: 大概是这个缘故，记得叔叔与政党也有关系。

en.t: Probably for that reason, I remember that my uncle also had connections with political parties.

units.source_text: 从这一点来看，叔叔虽然是父亲的胞弟，性格却与父亲截然不同。

en.t: In that respect, although my uncle was my father's own younger brother, his character was entirely different from my father's.

units.source_text: 父亲是个笃实本分的人，老老实实地守着继承的祖业。

en.t: My father was an honest and dutiful man who faithfully preserved the family estate he had inherited.

units.source_text: 他嗜好品茶插花，还喜欢读些诗歌什么的，

en.t: He enjoyed tea and flower arrangement, and he also liked reading poetry and the like,

units.source_text: 对于书画古董之类也颇有兴趣。

en.t: and he had considerable interest in calligraphy, paintings, antiques, and such things.

units.source_text: 我家在乡间，叔叔则住在相距大约二里远的市里。

en.t: Our house was in the countryside, while my uncle lived in a town about two ri away.

units.source_text: 市里旧家具店的掌柜常常专程带些字画、香炉之类的古董，拿来给父亲看。

en.t: The owner of an old furniture shop in town often made a special trip bringing antiques such as calligraphy, paintings, and incense burners for my father to examine.

units.source_text: 简而言之，父亲可以说是个man of means，

en.t: In short, my father could be called a man of means,

units.source_text: 算是个比较喜欢附庸风雅的乡绅。

en.t: a country gentleman with a rather strong taste for cultured pursuits.

units.source_text: 因此，就性情而论，和好交际的叔叔很不一样。

en.t: Therefore, in temperament, he was very different from my sociable uncle.

units.source_text: 然而，两个人的感情却相当好，父亲经常称赞叔叔是个远比自己有作为、可信赖的人。

en.t: Nevertheless, the two brothers were quite close, and my father often praised my uncle as a man far more capable and reliable than himself.

units.source_text: 还说像他自己这样继承了父母财产的人，天赋才干必然会迟钝。

en.t: He also said that a person like himself, who had inherited his parents' property, was bound to have his natural abilities dulled.

units.source_text: 换言之，因为无须与人竞争，所以才这样碌碌无为的。

en.t: In other words, because he had no need to compete with others, he had become so ineffectual.

units.source_text: 这些话，母亲听到过，我也听到过。

en.t: My mother heard these words, and I heard them too.

units.source_text: 我想父亲显然是说给我听的，希望我不要像他那样。

en.t: I think my father was clearly saying them for my benefit, hoping that I would not become like him.

units.source_text: ‘你要好好记住啊。’

en.t: You must remember this well.

units.source_text: 这句话，当时父亲是看着我说的，所以我一直没有忘掉。

en.t: My father looked at me when he said those words, so I have never forgotten them.

units.source_text: 我怎么能怀疑受到父亲如此信赖、称赞的叔叔呢？

en.t: How could I possibly doubt an uncle whom my father trusted and praised so highly?

units.source_text: 叔叔本来就是我引以为豪的人。

en.t: My uncle had always been someone I was proud of.

units.source_text: 对于父母去世后，一切都要仰仗其帮助的我来说，

en.t: For me, who after my parents' deaths had to rely on him for everything,

units.source_text: 叔叔已不仅仅是让我感到自豪的人，而且已是我人生中不可缺少的人了。

en.t: my uncle was no longer merely someone who made me proud; he had become indispensable to my life.
